what_i_see: A round, faint, uniform disc of light about 11 arcsec across with a faint point-like source near its middle and a fairly sharp edge. A brighter small galaxy lies 10 arcsec north. Only VIS data here; the colour panel has no near-infrared.
most_likely: A nucleated low-surface-brightness dwarf galaxy, possibly a satellite of the galaxy to the north.
against_it: Flat profile with abrupt edge near 5.7 arcsec, the same size as the j0259335 patch, could mean an optical ghost. No colour information to help.
decisive_test: Check individual dithered VIS exposures and DES/Legacy deep images for the same patch at the same sky position.
catalogue_notes: Nothing in SIMBAD within 60 arcsec or NED within 30. Legacy photo-z none within 5. Gaia none within 16; G=12.8 star at 86 (not distinctive). Four lens lists: no match within 60.
